questions.text_english:
(a) Explain the following elements of Marketing Mix:
(i) Product
(ii) Price
(iii) Promotion
OR
(b) Explain the following components of physical distribution:
(i) Order processing
(ii) Warehousing
(iii) Inventory control

sub_questions.text: उत्पाद

key_points: Product is the first P of marketing mix
It includes physical product, services, features, quality, branding, packaging

sub_questions.solution: Product refers to anything that can be offered to a market to satisfy a want or need. It is the most fundamental element of the marketing mix. A product includes the physical good itself as well as its associated features such as quality, design, brand name, packaging, labelling, warranty and after-sales service. When developing a product, marketers must carefully consider the needs and preferences of the target customers. The product must offer value and solve customer problems. Products can be goods, services, ideas, places or persons. Decisions about the product — its features, quality, design and branding — form the foundation on which all other marketing mix decisions (price, place, promotion) are built.

sub_questions.text: मूल्य

key_points: Price is the amount charged for a product
Only revenue-generating element of marketing mix
Influenced by cost, competition, demand, objectives

sub_questions.solution: Price refers to the amount of money that customers must pay to obtain the product. It is the only element of the marketing mix that generates revenue — all other elements represent costs. Pricing decisions are influenced by several factors including the cost of production, the level of competition, the demand and supply conditions, the pricing objectives of the company, and the perceived value of the product by consumers. Pricing strategies include cost-plus pricing, competition-based pricing, penetration pricing and skimming pricing. The price must be acceptable to customers (neither too high to deter purchase nor too low to undermine quality perception) while enabling the firm to earn adequate profit.

sub_questions.text: प्रवर्तन

key_points: Includes advertising, sales promotion, personal selling, public relations
Aims to inform, persuade and remind customers

sub_questions.solution: Promotion refers to all the activities undertaken by a company to communicate information about its products to potential customers and persuade them to make a purchase. It is the promotional mix or communications mix of the company. Promotion includes four main tools: advertising (paid non-personal communication through mass media), personal selling (direct face-to-face communication by salespersons), sales promotion (short-term incentives like discounts, contests, coupons), and public relations (building a positive image through press releases, events and sponsorships). The objectives of promotion are to inform customers about the product, persuade them to buy it, and remind existing customers about the brand to maintain their loyalty.

sub_questions.text: आदेश का प्रक्रियण

key_points: Series of steps from receiving order to delivery
Includes receiving, recording, filling and dispatching orders

sub_questions.solution: Order processing refers to the entire set of activities that begin when a customer places an order and end when the goods are delivered to the customer. It includes receiving the order, checking the order for accuracy and availability of stock, recording the order in the system, arranging for the goods to be picked from the warehouse, packing and dispatching them to the delivery address. Efficient order processing reduces the time between order placement and delivery (the order cycle time), which directly impacts customer satisfaction. Poor order processing leads to delays, errors, and unhappy customers, harming the company's reputation and business.

sub_questions.text: भंडारण

key_points: Bridges gap between production and consumption

sub_questions.solution: Warehousing refers to the activities involved in storing goods from the time of production until the time of sale or use. It bridges the gap between production and consumption by holding inventory so that goods are available when customers need them. Warehousing creates time utility — goods produced in advance are stored and made available at the right time. Warehouses can be owned by the company (private warehouses) or rented from third-party providers (public warehouses). Modern warehouses are equipped with refrigeration, security systems and inventory management software. Efficient warehousing reduces lead times, ensures product availability and helps companies meet customer demand without stockouts.

sub_questions.text: संगृहीत माल (इन्वेन्ट्री) पर नियन्त्रण

key_points: Managing stock levels to avoid excess or shortage
Tools: Economic Order Quantity, ABC analysis, Just-in-Time

sub_questions.solution: Inventory control refers to the process of managing the levels of stock held in the warehouse to ensure that sufficient quantities are available to meet customer demand without holding excessive amounts that tie up capital and increase storage costs. The objective is to maintain the optimum level of inventory — not too much (to avoid high holding costs, obsolescence and wastage) and not too little (to avoid stockouts and lost sales). Tools used for inventory control include Economic Order Quantity (EOQ) — the optimal order size that minimises total inventory costs; ABC Analysis — categorising items by value for priority management; and Just-In-Time (JIT) inventory — receiving goods only when needed in the production process, reducing holding costs.

key_points: Three Marketing Mix elements OR three physical distribution components explained

questions.solution:
Answer for part (a): (i) Product — anything offered to satisfy a want, including features, quality, design, brand and packaging; must fulfil customer needs and forms the foundation of the marketing mix. (ii) Price — the amount charged for the product; the only revenue-generating element; determined by cost, competition, demand and company objectives. (iii) Promotion — communication activities including advertising, personal selling, sales promotion and public relations aimed at informing, persuading and reminding customers.

Answer for part (b): (i) Order processing — activities from receiving an order to its delivery, including recording, picking, packing and dispatching; affects customer satisfaction and order cycle time. (ii) Warehousing — storing goods between production and consumption to create time utility and ensure availability when needed. (iii) Inventory control — maintaining optimum stock levels to balance holding costs against stockout risks, using tools such as EOQ, ABC analysis and JIT.
